# Diagnosing and Replacing the Camshaft Position Switch on a 2011 Chevy Equinox

Seeing the check engine light illuminate on a 2011 Chevrolet Equinox is often an immediate cue for the vehicle's powertrain control module (PCM) that it has lost synchronization with the camshaft. When the diagnostic trouble code P0013 appears, the system has specifically identified a problem with Circuit B of the Intake Camshaft Position Actuator "A" on Bank 1. While this error frequently points to a failing solenoid, the repair strategy requires distinguishing between an electrical fault and a mechanical binding issue before swapping components.

The actuator itself is an electrically operated hydraulic solenoid responsible for adjusting the timing of the intake camshaft. In many GM Direct Injection (DI) engines found in this model year, these units are notorious for failing not because they stop receiving power, but because the internal valve sticks open or closed due to oil sludge or debris accumulation. If you simply replace a faulty solenoid without addressing the root causeâdirty engine oilâthe new unit will likely fail within days or weeks. Therefore, the replacement procedure mandates a complete oil change and an inspection of the intake valves for carbon buildup that could prevent the actuator from achieving full stroke travel.

### Accessing the Component

Accessing the camshaft position switch and actuator on the 2011 Equinox requires careful removal of the engine cover and often the upper intake manifold runners. The location is typically tucked behind the plenum, making visual inspection difficult without disassembly. Before removing any bolts, you must disconnect the negative battery terminal to prevent accidental short circuits or unintended fuel pump activation while working near high-pressure lines.

Once the area is exposed, locate the actuator mounted directly on the timing chain cover near the camshaft journal. You will need to remove the electrical connector and the retaining bolt. The solenoid can be lifted straight up, but take care not to drop debris into the intake port or timing cover cavity. If you are replacing the switch (the sensor that detects cam position) rather than the actuator, ensure you have a replacement part that matches the specific resistance specifications for your VIN, as GM has updated these components over the production run of this model year.

### Installation and Verification

Installing the new component involves reversing the removal steps, but the critical phase is post-installation verification. After reconnecting the battery and starting the engine, listen closely to the area where the actuator was mounted. A healthy replacement will produce a distinct clicking sound as it adjusts the camshaft timing upon cold start and during driving transitions. If you hear a continuous whine or silence followed by rough idle, the new unit may be defective or the oil clearance is insufficient.

There are no specific diagnostic commands to reset the P0013 code immediately after replacement; the PCM must learn the new camshaft position relative to the crankshaft during several drive cycles. However, if you utilize a professional scan tool capable of live data streaming, you can monitor the "Cam Actuator Duty Cycle" parameter. A sudden drop or spike in this percentage reading compared to baseline data suggests the new actuator is still encountering resistance or that the oil pressure is insufficient to move the camshaft fully.

If the issue persists after replacing both the sensor and the solenoid, the problem may lie deeper within the engine's mechanical architecture, such as a bent timing chain or a failing lifters on Bank 1. In such cases, further investigation into the hydraulic roller system is required before declaring the electrical components fully functional.
